literature.headline_zh: 汉坦病毒本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期汉坦病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: 在前瞻性系列研究中,70%的NE患者在急性期报告了眼部症状,其中88%出现眼内压降低,87%视力下降,87%结膜水肿,82%晶状体增厚,78%出现近视性屈光变化,64%前房变浅,52%玻璃体长度缩短。 [10.1038/s41433-026-04848-9]
本研究发现,汉坦病毒 感染在儿科患者中表现出特定的影像学特征,但由于可能出现假阳性结果,不应仅凭影像学特征进行诊断,需结合临床表现。 [10.1007/s10140-026-02535-6]
基本再生数估计为 R 0 = 2.30 (95% CI: 1.33–3.27),表明人类传播具有持续性。不确定性与敏感性分析显示,传染性及潜伏期的变化主要影响暴发的时间和规模,而超级传播事件可显著改变疫情进化的传播动态。 [10.64898/2026.08.31.26361797]
在汉坦病毒肺综合征(HCPS)病例中,根据感染的严重程度,及时给予退热药、血管加压药、补液治疗、心肺支持、体外膜肺氧合(ECMO)、机械通气和肾脏替代治疗(RRT)非常重要。 [10.1186/s12985-026-03298-9]
literature.trend_or_risk_zh: 本期研究方向以入选文献实际覆盖的临床、流行病学、宿主生态、诊断或分子监测主题为准。
literature.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments.
key_findings_en: In the prospective series, 70% of NE patients reported ocular symptoms during acute illness, with 88% experiencing decreased IOP, 87% reduced visual acuity, 87% conjunctival chemosis, 82% crystalline lens thickening, 78% a myopic shift, 64% anterior chamber shallowing, and 52% shortened vitreous length. [10.1038/s41433-026-04848-9]

The study found that hantavirus infection in pediatric patients presents with specific imaging features, but these should not be the sole basis for diagnosis due to the potential for false positives and the need for clinical correlation. [10.1007/s10140-026-02535-6]
The editorial does not report any specific results or data. [10.1080/08998280.2026.2720843]
The reproduction number was estimated at R 0 = 2.30 (95% CI: 1.33–3.27), indicating sustained human transmission. [10.64898/2026.08.31.26361797]

In cases of HCPS, depending on the severity of the infection, it is important to administer antipyretics, vasopressors, fluid therapy, cardiopulmonary support, extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO), mechanical ventilation, and renal replacement therapy (RRT) in a timely manner. [10.1186/s12985-026-03298-9]

papers.title: Incidence, pathogenesis, clinical manifestations, and pharmacological management of the 2026 Andes virus outbreak.
papers.abstract: Hantavirus is considered as a fatal zoonotic pathogen that can be commonly transmitted from rodents to humans. However, the Andes virus (ANDV), a type of New World hantavirus, can also be transmitted from human to human. It is the cause of the 2026 hantavirus outbreak on a cruise ship. Hantavirus can rapidly progress to a severe respiratory distress, known as hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome (HCPS). Since there is no specific treatment or approved vaccine for hantavirus infection, early diagnosis and critical care support are essential. In cases of HCPS, depending on the severity of the infection, it is important to administer antipyretics, vasopressors, fluid therapy, cardiopulmonary support, extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO), mechanical ventilation, and renal replacement therapy (RRT) in a timely manner. Currently, there is no approved vaccine in the United States or Europe. However, various vaccine technologies, including inactivated, DNA, mRNA, viral vector and protein-based vaccines, are in the preclinical and clinical phases. Preventive actions, including patient isolation and physical distancing, are crucial to avoiding widespread transmission.

papers.title: Andes Hantavirus human-to-human transmission dynamics and1 preparedness scenarios
papers.abstract: Abstract Human-to-human transmission of the Andes virus (ANDV), which causes the deadly Hantavirus Pulmonary Syndrome, has been documented in several outbreaks, but remains insufficiently characterized to ensure preparedness against future emergence. Here, we integrate epidemiological data from historical outbreaks and from the 2026 MV Hondius outbreak with a stochastic network-based transmission model to quantify ANDV epidemic potential and control requirements. We estimate a reproduction number of R 0 = 2.30 (95% CI: 1.33–3.27), supporting sustained human transmission. Uncertainty and sensitivity analysis show that variation in transmissibility and incubation period mainly affects outbreak timing and size, while superspreading events can substantially alter the epidemic evolution. Model analysis and simulations further reveal how contact-network structure strongly modulates outbreak size, with close-contact clustering facilitating containment. Due to the virus characteristics, rapid identification and isolation can effectively suppress outbreaks, even more effectively than in the case of COVID-19, whereas pre-symptomatic transmission or increased mixing could substantially increase risk. Our results provide a quantitative framework for ANDV preparedness and highlight the most critical transmission features for future surveillance.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to understand the dynamics of human-to-human transmission of the Andes virus (ANDV), which causes Hantavirus Pulmonary Syndrome, to improve preparedness against future outbreaks.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study integrated epidemiological data from historical outbreaks and the 2026 MV Hondius outbreak with a stochastic network-based transmission model to quantify ANDV epidemic potential and control requirements.
analysis.methods: The researchers used a stochastic network-based transmission model and combined it with epidemiological data from historical outbreaks and the 2026 MV Hondius outbreak to estimate the reproduction number and assess transmission dynamics.
analysis.main_results: The reproduction number was estimated at R 0 = 2.30 (95% CI: 1.33–3.27), indicating sustained human transmission. Uncertainty and sensitivity analysis showed that transmissibility and incubation period variations mainly affect outbreak timing and size, while superspreading events can significantly alter epidemic evolution.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The model analysis and simulations revealed that contact-network structure strongly modulates outbreak size, with close-contact clustering facilitating containment, offering new insights into ANDV transmission dynamics.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings provide a quantitative framework for ANDV preparedness and highlight the most critical transmission features for future surveillance and intervention strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study relies on historical and outbreak data, which may introduce uncertainty, and the model assumptions could affect the generalizability of results. The evidence strength is moderate due to these limitations.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the human-to-human transmission dynamics of the Andes virus (ANDV), which causes Hantavirus Pulmonary Syndrome, to enhance preparedness against future outbreaks. By integrating historical and recent outbreak data with a stochastic network-based transmission model, the researchers estimated the reproduction number (R 0 = 2.30, 95% CI: 1.33–3.27), indicating sustained human transmission. Their analysis showed that variations in transmissibility and incubation period mainly affect outbreak timing and size, while superspreading events can significantly alter epidemic evolution. The study also found that close-contact clustering in networks can facilitate containment. These results offer a quantitative framework for ANDV preparedness and emphasize the importance of understanding transmission features for effective surveillance. However, the reliance on historical data and model assumptions limits the generalizability of findings, resulting in moderate evidence strength.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在了解安第斯病毒(ANDV)导致的汉坦病毒肺综合征(汉坦病毒肺综合征,HPS)的人传人传播动态,以提高对未来疫情的准备能力。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究整合了历史暴发和2026年MV Hondius暴发的流行病学数据,并结合基于随机网络的传播模型,以量化ANDV疫情的传播潜力和控制需求。
elements_zh.methods: 研究人员使用基于随机网络的传播模型,并结合历史暴发和2026年MV Hondius暴发的流行病学数据,以估计基本再生数并评估传播动态。
elements_zh.main_results: 基本再生数估计为 R 0 = 2.30 (95% CI: 1.33–3.27),表明人类传播具有持续性。不确定性与敏感性分析显示,传染性及潜伏期的变化主要影响暴发的时间和规模,而超级传播事件可显著改变疫情进化的传播动态。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 模型分析和模拟揭示了接触网络结构对疫情规模的强烈调节作用,紧密接触的集群有助于控制疫情,为ANDV传播动态提供了新的见解。

papers.title: Network-Guided Drug Repurposing for Hantavirus Infection: Pathway Analysis, Target Identification, and Molecular What-If Simulations
papers.abstract: Hantaviruses cause haemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome and hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome, together responsible for more than 200,000 cases annually, but no specific antiviral therapy is approved. We developed a three-stage computational framework for systematic drug repurposing. Transcriptomic analysis of Hantaan virus-infected human umbilical vein endothelial cells (GEO GSE133751) identified 203 differentially expressed genes dominated by interferon-stimulated genes. A STRING protein–protein interaction network (176 nodes, 3,210 edges) and composite master-regulator centrality score identified 15 hubs, including ISG15, IRF1, CXCL10, STAT1, and DDX58. Open Targets analysis identified six druggable hubs and 12 repurposing candidates in four priority tiers. An ordinary differential equation model of type I interferon signalling then evaluated eight drug perturbations. Early IFN-β achieved the fastest viral clearance (3.5 days) with reduced CXCL10 immunopathology. Early JAK inhibition delayed clearance (4.9 days) and increased CXCL10, an effect that follows from modelling CXCL10 as an IRF1-driven rather than STAT1-driven output. Combining IFN-β with an anti-CXCL10 monoclonal antibody produced the best balance between antiviral efficacy and immunopathology control, although in the present model the antiviral gain of this combination derives entirely from its interferon component. This mechanistically grounded, evidence-ranked framework prioritises candidate therapies and phase-specific combinations for preclinical hantavirus studies.

analysis.summary_en: This study presents a computational framework for drug repurposing targeting hantaviruses, which cause significant human diseases such as hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome and hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome. The framework combines transcriptomic analysis of Hantaan virus-infected cells with network-based methods to identify key molecular targets and potential therapies. The results highlight 15 hub genes in the interferon response pathway, with six being druggable. The study evaluates drug perturbations, showing that early IFN-β treatment leads to rapid viral clearance and reduced immunopathology. However, the model indicates that the antiviral effect of combining IFN-β with an anti-CXCL10 monoclonal antibody is primarily due to the interferon component. The findings offer a mechanistically grounded approach for prioritizing candidate therapies and combinations for preclinical hantavirus research, but the study is limited to computational models without direct clinical validation.

papers.source_body_en: Hantaviruses cause haemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome and hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome, together responsible for more than 200,000 cases annually, but no specific antiviral therapy is approved. papers.abstract_zh: 汉坦病毒 感染可导致肾综合征出血热和汉坦病毒肺综合征,每年共同造成超过 200,000 例病例,但目前尚无获批的特定 抗病毒药物 治疗方案。我们开发了一个三阶段的计算框架,用于系统性药物再利用。对汉坦病毒感染的人脐静脉内皮细胞(GEO GSE133751)进行转录组分析,鉴定了 203 个差异表达基因,其中以干扰素刺激基因为主导。STRING 蛋白-蛋白相互作用网络(176 个节点,3,210 条边)和复合主调控因子中心性评分鉴定了 15 个枢纽基因,包括 ISG15、IRF1、CXCL10、STAT1 和 DDX58。Open Targets 分析确定了四个优先级层级中的六个可药用枢纽基因和 12 个药物再利用候选药物。随后,利用 I 型干扰素信号的普通微分方程模型评估了八种药物干预。早期 IFN-β 实现了最快的病毒清除(3.5 天),并减少了 CXCL10 的免疫病理效应。早期 JAK 抑制剂则延迟了病毒清除(4.9 天)并增加了 CXCL10,这一效应源于将 CXCL10 模型为 IRF1 驱动而非 STAT1 驱动的输出。将 IFN-β 与抗 CXCL10 单克隆抗体联合使用,在 抗病毒药物 有效性与免疫病理控制之间取得了最佳平衡,尽管在当前模型中,该组合的 抗病毒药物 效益完全来自于其干扰素成分。这种基于机制且有证据支持的框架,为预临床汉坦病毒研究优先考虑候选治疗方案和阶段特异性组合。

papers.full_text: Subjects Emerging infectious disease preparedness has traditionally focused on emergency medicine, infectious disease, and critical care specialists. However, the ophthalmologist is not insulated from emerging infectious disease. The 2026 Andes virus outbreak highlights why ophthalmologists should also be incorporated into outbreak surveillance and response. Throughout history, ophthalmologists have played an important role in identifying infectious diseases through their ocular manifestations. Yet, this role depends on a clear understanding of a pathogen’s ophthalmic phenotype. Despite growing attention surrounding the current Andes virus outbreak, the ocular manifestations of this pathogen remain largely undefined. This knowledge gap presents both an opportunity and a responsibility for ophthalmologists to systematically characterise ocular involvement and contribute to emerging infectious disease surveillance. Herein, we review the available evidence regarding ocular involvement in hantavirus infection and contend that ophthalmologists have a critical role in defining the ocular phenotype of Andes virus during the current outbreak. The Andes strain of Hantavirus was recently documented aboard an international vessel. In April 2026, passengers and crew aboard the MV Hondius, began developing severe respiratory illness during an itinerary across the South Atlantic. The World Health Organization was notified on May 2, 2026, and Andes virus was confirmed as the causative pathogen on May 5 [1]. As of late-May 2026, 13 confirmed or probable cases and 3 deaths had been reported across multiple countries, with the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) monitoring several individuals across multiple US states [2]. Although the overall public health risk in the United States remains low, the CDC has issued a Health Alert Network advisory emphasising heightened clinical vigilance. Hantaviruses (family Hantaviridae) are enveloped, single-stranded, negative-sense RNA viruses transmitted primarily through aerosolisation of infected rodent excrement, causing two principal syndromes: hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS) from New World hantaviruses including Sin Nombre and Andes viruses, and haemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) from Old World hantaviruses such as Puumala, Hantaan, and Seoul viruses. Andes virus is the only hantavirus with recently confirmed person-to-person transmission, typically via respiratory secretions during prolonged close contact with a symptomatic individual [3]. The ophthalmic literature on hantavirus is dominated by Puumala virus, which causes nephropathia epidemica (NE), a generally mild to moderate, renal-predominant form of HFRS. In the largest prospective ophthalmic series to date, Hautala et al. examined 92 eyes of 46 serologically confirmed NE patients and found that 70% reported ocular symptoms during acute illness, with decreased IOP in 88%, reduced visual acuity in 87%, conjunctival chemosis in 87%, crystalline lens thickening in 82%, a myopic shift in 78%, anterior chamber shallowing in 64%, and shortened vitreous length in 52% [4]. All anterior segment changes resolved fully with systemic recovery. Transient myopia is the hallmark finding, occasionally exceeding −4.0 diopters [5]. External findings include periorbital oedema, conjunctival injection, and subconjunctival haemorrhage [4,5,6]. Posterior findings are less frequent but include retinal haemorrhages, macular oedema, retinal whitening near the optic disc, and a self-limiting posterior necrotising retinitis, with neuro-ophthalmic manifestations possible when CNS complications such as hypophyseal haemorrhage occur [5]. Although ocular manifestations of Puumala strain of hantavirus infection are well described, virtually no ophthalmic data exist for Andes virus, the pathogen responsible for the current outbreak. This distinction is critical because existing ophthalmic knowledge is derived from a different virus, a different clinical syndrome, and a substantially different severity spectrum. What we do know is that in contrast to the Puumala virus, the systemic manifestations of the Andes virus causes HPS, a fulminant cardiopulmonary illness in which patients progress rapidly to respiratory failure, mechanical ventilation, and in severe cases extracorporeal support [7]. To date, no ophthalmic evaluation of HPS patients has been published. This gap in knowledge has practical consequences. Clinically, this means that the pattern of presentation that ophthalmologists may be tasked to recognise is extrapolated from a population that differs in virus, syndrome severity, and clinical state. The existing literature on the Puumala virus may be used to prompt suspicion (i.e., a febrile patient with bilateral unexplained myopic shift should raise the possibility of hantavirus), but it cannot yet tell ophthalmologists what Andes virus ocular disease looks like beyond that. The current outbreak represents not only a clinical challenge but also a scientific opportunity. For ophthalmologists, this means that every HPS patient managed at a US referral centre during the current outbreak who is well enough to undergo ophthalmic evaluation represents an opportunity to generate evidence that does not yet exist. A standardised assessment, documented and reported in the literature, would begin to answer a question that the existing literature cannot. Importantly, ophthalmologists should examine patients with known or suspected hantavirus using correct transmission-based precautions. Unlike other hantaviruses, Andes virus has documented person-to-person transmission via respiratory secretions, a characteristic with no known analogue among other hantaviruses. For ophthalmologists, this distinction is particularly relevant because slit-lamp examination requires prolonged face-to-face proximity. Consequently, infection-control preparedness should be considered. The CDC recommends airborne infection isolation with gown, gloves, eye protection, and an N95 or higher-level respirator for any patient with confirmed or suspected infection [2]. Historically, ophthalmologists have contributed immensely to the recognition and characterisation of systemic infectious diseases through their ocular manifestations. From syphilis and tuberculosis to more recent outbreaks involving Zika virus, Mpox, and COVID-19, ocular findings have occasionally provided diagnostic clues, insight into disease pathogenesis, and opportunities for longitudinal monitoring. The Andes virus should be viewed within this broader framework. The 2026 Andes virus outbreak carries with it a powerful lesson. We as ophthalmologists are not peripheral observers during emerging infectious disease events. We contribute to surveillance, diagnosis, characterisation of novel ocular manifestations, and implementation of appropriate infection-control practices. As the outbreak evolves, systematic ophthalmic evaluation of affected patients may help close a major knowledge gap regarding the ocular manifestations of the Hantavirus Andes strain infection. analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to highlight the need for ophthalmic vigilance during the 2026 Hantavirus outbreak, as traditional preparedness efforts have focused on emergency medicine, infectious disease, and critical care specialists.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study reviewed the available evidence regarding ocular involvement in hantavirus infection, with a focus on the Andes virus outbreak on the MV Hondius in April 2026, which led to 13 confirmed or probable cases and 3 deaths across multiple countries.
analysis.methods: The study examined the ophthalmic literature, particularly focusing on Puumala virus, which causes nephropathia epidemica, and included a prospective series of 46 patients with serologically confirmed NE, analyzing 92 eyes for ocular manifestations.
analysis.main_results: In the prospective series, 70% of NE patients reported ocular symptoms during acute illness, with 88% experiencing decreased IOP, 87% reduced visual acuity, 87% conjunctival chemosis, 82% crystalline lens thickening, 78% a myopic shift, 64% anterior chamber shallowing, and 52% shortened vitreous length.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that ophthalmologists have a critical role in defining the ocular phenotype of Andes virus during the current outbreak, as the ocular manifestations of this pathogen remain largely undefined despite growing attention.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform the importance of ophthalmologists in surveillance and response to hantavirus outbreaks, particularly for identifying ocular involvement in Andes virus infections and contributing to broader infectious disease monitoring.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its focus on Puumala virus and the lack of specific data on Andes virus ocular manifestations, though it provides a foundation for understanding the potential role of ophthalmologists in hantavirus surveillance. The evidence is moderate in strength.

analysis.summary_en: This study emphasizes the need for ophthalmic vigilance during the 2026 Hantavirus outbreak, particularly highlighting the role of ophthalmologists in identifying ocular manifestations of the virus. The research reviews existing literature on hantavirus ocular involvement, noting that while Puumala virus has been extensively studied, the ocular phenotype of Andes virus remains undefined. A prospective series of 46 patients with nephropathia epidemica (NE) revealed significant ocular symptoms, including decreased IOP, reduced visual acuity, and conjunctival chemosis. These findings suggest that ophthalmologists can play a critical role in defining the ocular phenotype of Andes virus during the outbreak. However, the study's focus on Puumala virus and lack of direct data on Andes virus ocular involvement limit its strength, though the evidence is considered moderate. The results underscore the importance of integrating ophthalmic expertise into broader infectious disease surveillance efforts.

papers.title_zh: 2026年汉坦病毒 暴发期间眼部警惕性的理由。
papers.source_body_en: Herein, we review the available evidence regarding ocular involvement in hantavirus infection and contend that ophthalmologists have a critical role in defining the ocular phenotype of Andes virus during the current outbreak. Transient myopia is the hallmark finding, occasionally exceeding −4.0 diopters [5]. External findings include periorbital oedema, conjunctival injection, and subconjunctival haemorrhage [4,5,6]. Posterior findings are less frequent but include retinal haemorrhages, macular oedema, retinal whitening near the optic disc, and a self-limiting posterior necrotising retinitis, with neuro-ophthalmic manifestations possible when CNS complications such as hypophyseal haemorrhage occur [5]. From syphilis and tuberculosis to more recent outbreaks involving Zika virus, Mpox, and COVID-19, ocular findings have occasionally provided diagnostic clues, insight into disease pathogenesis, and opportunities for longitudinal monitoring. Prospective study on ocular findings in acute Puumala hantavirus infection in hospitalised patients. Subjects Emerging infectious disease preparedness has traditionally focused on emergency medicine, infectious disease, and critical care specialists. However, the ophthalmologist is not insulated from emerging infectious disease. The 2026 Andes virus outbreak highlights why ophthalmologists should also be incorporated into outbreak surveillance and response. Throughout history, ophthalmologists have played an important role in identifying infectious diseases through their ocular manifestations. Yet, this role depends on a clear understanding of a pathogen’s ophthalmic phenotype. Despite growing attention surrounding the current Andes virus outbreak, the ocular manifestations of this pathogen remain largely undefined. This knowledge gap...

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在强调在2026年汉坦病毒 暴发期间需要加强眼科警惕性,因为传统的应急准备工作主要集中在急诊医学、传染病和重症监护专科领域。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究回顾了有关汉坦病毒感染中眼部受累的现有证据,重点关注2026年4月在MV Hondius暴发的Andes病毒暴发,导致多个国家出现13例确诊病例或疑似病例,并造成3人死亡。
analysis_zh.methods: 该研究查阅了眼科文献,特别关注了引起肾综合征出血热的汉坦病毒Puumala亚型,并纳入了46例血清学确诊的NE患者前瞻性系列,分析了92只眼睛的眼部表现。
analysis_zh.main_results: 在前瞻性系列研究中,70%的NE患者在急性期报告了眼部症状,其中88%出现眼内压降低,87%视力下降,87%结膜水肿,82%晶状体增厚,78%出现近视性屈光变化,64%前房变浅,52%玻璃体长度缩短。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者认为,在当前暴发期间,眼科医生在定义安第斯病毒的眼部表型方面起着关键作用,因为尽管该病原体日益受到关注,其眼部表现仍 largely undefined。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现强调了眼科医生在监测和应对汉坦病毒 暴发中的重要性,特别是在识别安第斯病毒感染中的眼部受累情况以及参与更广泛的传染病监测方面。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的局限性在于其仅关注Puumala病毒,且缺乏关于Andes病毒眼部表现的具体数据,尽管它为理解眼科医生在监测中的潜在作用提供了基础。证据强度中等。

papers.title: Outbreak of Andes Virus Infection on Board MV Hondius, April – May 2026: Lessons for Biosafety Preparedness
papers.abstract: In April 2026, an outbreak of hantavirus infection caused by Andes virus (Orthohantavirus andesense) was reported on the expedition vessel MV Hondius, which had departed from the port of Ushuaia, Argentina, on 1 April 2026. Clinical symptoms in the first affected passenger appeared on 6 April, and the patient died on board the vessel on 11 April. In the following weeks, severe cases were identified among passengers and crew members after some individuals had disembarked and subsequently travelled through several countries. To assess the epidemiological and genomic characteristics of the outbreak and identify lessons for biosafety systems. Materials and Methods . We analyzed data from the epidemiological investigation provided by WHO and national health authorities. Genomic sequencing was performed using metagenomic approaches, SISPA, and hybridization enrichment. Phylogenetic analysis was conducted using the maximum likelihood method in IQ-TREE 3. Results and Discussion. Following outbreak investigation and diagnostic testing of patients in different countries, a total of 13 cases of infection were identified including 11 laboratory-confirmed cases, 2 probable cases, and 3 deaths. The epidemiological investigation suggests primary zoonotic infection of the index patient before boarding the vessel in an endemic area of southern Argentina, followed by limited person-to-person transmission on board. Genomic analysis demonstrated a high degree of identity among viral sequences obtained from affected individuals, which is consistent with a single introduction followed by subsequent human-to-human transmission. The hantavirus outbreak on board MV Hondius represents an important example of an epidemiologically significant event in which a zoonotic pathogen with limited capacity for person-to-person transmission occurred within a closed international community. This event highlights the importance of early clinical diagnosis, sanitary and quarantine measures for contact persons, and rapid international exchange of genomic data to ensure biosafety during epidemic events caused by emerging, rare, or genetically altered pathogens.

papers.abstract_zh: 2026年4月,一艘名为MV Hondius的探险船发生了一起由安第斯病毒(Orthohantavirus andesense)引起的暴发感染暴发事件。该船于2026年4月1日从阿根廷乌斯怀亚港出发。第一位受影响乘客的临床症状出现在4月6日,患者于4月11日船上传播死亡。在随后几周内,一些乘客和船员在下船后前往多个国家,相继出现了严重病例。为评估暴发的流行病学和基因组特征,并识别生物安全系统的经验教训。材料与方法:我们分析了世界卫生组织和国家卫生当局提供的流行病学调查数据。采用宏基因组方法、SISPA和杂交富集技术进行基因组测序。使用IQ-TREE 3的极大似然法进行系统发育分析。结果与讨论:在对不同国家患者进行暴发调查和诊断测试后,共确认了13例感染病例,包括11例实验室确诊病例、2例可能病例和3例死亡。流行病学调查显示,首发病例在登船前已在阿根廷南部的疫区发生动物源性感染,随后在船上出现了有限的人际传播。基因组分析显示,受影响个体的病毒序列具有高度同源性,这与单一引入后发生的人际传播一致。MV Hondius上的汉坦病毒 暴发事件是人兽共患病在封闭国际社区中发生的重要流行病学事件案例,该病原体具有有限的人际传播能力。这一事件凸显了早期临床诊断、对接触者的卫生和检疫措施,以及在由新兴、罕见或基因改变病原体引发的疫情中快速交换基因组数据的重要性。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 为评估该感染暴发的流行病学和基因组特征,并识别对生物安全系统的启示。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 在对不同国家患者进行感染暴发调查和诊断检测后,共确认了13例感染病例,包括11例实验室确诊病例、2例可能病例和3例死亡。

analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: MV Hondius号邮轮上的感染暴发代表了一个重要的流行病学事件案例,其中一种具有有限人际传播能力的人兽共患病原体在封闭的国际社区中出现。

papers.title_original: Pediatric hantavirus in emergency radiology: recognition without overreliance on imaging.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to address the recognition of hantavirus in emergency radiology without overreliance on imaging, highlighting the need for improved diagnostic approaches in pediatric cases.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study is a Letter that reviews previously published literature on hantavirus infection in emergency radiology, focusing on pediatric patients and their clinical presentations.
analysis.methods: The study relied on a systematic review of existing literature, including references to prior research on hantavirus pulmonary syndrome and cardiopulmonary syndrome in children, without generating new data.
analysis.main_results: The study found that hantavirus infection in pediatric patients presents with specific imaging features, but these should not be the sole basis for diagnosis due to the potential for false positives and the need for clinical correlation.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that while imaging can aid in recognizing hantavirus infection, it should be used cautiously and in conjunction with clinical findings, emphasizing the novelty of this perspective in emergency radiology.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform emergency radiologists about the importance of integrating clinical judgment with imaging findings to avoid misdiagnosis and ensure appropriate management of hantavirus infections in children.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on previously published literature and lacks original data, resulting in moderate evidence strength.

analysis.summary_en: This study, a Letter, addresses the recognition of hantavirus in emergency radiology, particularly in pediatric patients, without overreliance on imaging. It reviews existing literature on hantavirus pulmonary syndrome and cardiopulmonary syndrome in children, emphasizing the need for clinical correlation. The authors interpret that while imaging can aid in identifying hantavirus infection, it should not be the sole diagnostic tool. The study highlights the importance of integrating clinical findings with imaging to avoid misdiagnosis and improve management of hantavirus infections in children. However, the study is limited by its reliance on previously published literature and lacks original data, resulting in moderate evidence strength.

papers.title: AI-generated medical realism and hantavirus misinformation: a new public health threat?
papers.abstract: The widespread availability of generative artificial intelligence (AI) has substantially reshaped the health-information environment compared with the COVID-19 pandemic. Contemporary AI tools can rapidly generate highly realistic medical-looking content from text, including laboratory reports, radiological images, histological slides, and institutional clinical documentation. During infectious disease outbreaks, such simulated medical content may exploit the visual authority traditionally associated with healthcare institutions and influence public risk perception. During media coverage of the May 2026 Andes virus (ANDV) alert in Italy, news outlets published realistic AI-generated medical imagery depicting hantavirus diagnostic reports, hospital-associated laboratory materials, and outbreak-response scenes linked to real healthcare institutions. One image, in particular, reproduced the visual identity of a real laboratory report produced at “Luigi Sacco” University Hospital despite displaying multiple inconsistencies. In some additional examples, AI generation was not clearly disclosed despite the use of recognizable institutional names and logos. This phenomenon has the potential to extend beyond isolated misinformation events. Emerging evidence indicates that experts may struggle to reliably distinguish AI-generated biomedical and radiological images from authentic materials, raising concern that future infectious disease outbreaks may occur within an information ecosystem increasingly shaped by visually persuasive synthetic media. Such content may amplify public anxiety, distort perceptions of authority, and erode trust in institutions. Synthetic medical realism should therefore be considered a potential emerging category of public-health risk during infectious disease emergencies that requires coordinated action from institutions and regulators developing verification systems, while news media, platforms, and publishers implement AI-disclosure standards and guidelines for synthetic biomedical content.

In some additional examples, AI generation was not clearly disclosed despite the use of recognizable institutional names and logos. This phenomenon has the potential to extend beyond isolated misinformation events. Emerging evidence indicates that experts may struggle to reliably distinguish AI-generated biomedical and radiological images from authentic materials, raising concern that future infectious disease outbreaks may occur within an information ecosystem increasingly shaped by visually persuasive synthetic media. Such content may amplify public anxiety, distort perceptions of authority, and erode trust in institutions. Synthetic medical realism should therefore be considered a potential emerging category of public-health risk during infectious disease emergencies that requires coordinated action from institutions and regulators developing verification systems, while news media, platforms, and publishers implement AI-disclosure standards and guidelines for synthetic biomedical content.

papers.title: Central nervous system involvement of hantaviruses: clinical presentations, neuroimaging findings, and current implications.
papers.abstract: Abstract Because of their involvement in outbreaks, hantaviruses as emerging zoonotic diseases have been regarded a public health issue. Recent reports have identified CNS symptoms of hantavirus infection, although the data are still relatively sparse and inconsistent, especially for Andes orthohantavirus (ANDV) and to a lesser extent Puumala virus (PUUV). Reported neurological features include headache, dizziness, altered mental state, seizures, focal deficits, and peripheral neuropathy, possibly accompanied by ocular symptoms such as impaired vision and photophobia. The results of neuroimaging have been inconsistent and nonspecific, ranging from hemorrhagic or edematous changes to thalamic or brainstem abnormalities and splenial lesions. Evidence could suggest that endothelial dysfunction, capillary leak, inflammatory damage, and, in certain situations, potential intrathecal immunological responses or direct viral presence may all contribute to CNS involvement. However, most evidence stems from case reports or case series, and causative neuroinvasion may not have been fully demonstrated. Recent studies, especially the recent ANDV-associated outbreak, may emphasize the necessity for rigorous neurological examination. A better understanding of the neurological range of hantavirus infection may enhance detection, risk stratification, and supportive therapy.

Reported neurological features include headache, dizziness, altered mental state, seizures, focal deficits, and peripheral neuropathy, possibly accompanied by ocular symptoms such as impaired vision and photophobia. The results of neuroimaging have been inconsistent and nonspecific, ranging from hemorrhagic or edematous changes to thalamic or brainstem abnormalities and splenial lesions. Evidence could suggest that endothelial dysfunction, capillary leak, inflammatory damage, and, in certain situations, potential intrathecal immunological responses or direct viral presence may all contribute to CNS involvement. However, most evidence stems from case reports or case series, and causative neuroinvasion may not have been fully demonstrated. Recent studies, especially the recent ANDV-associated outbreak, may emphasize the necessity for rigorous neurological examination. A better understanding of the neurological range of hantavirus infection may enhance detection, risk stratification, and supportive therapy.

elements_zh.methods: 该研究是对现有文献的综述,重点聚焦于病例报告及其系列。它探讨了临床表现、神经影像学发现以及汉坦病毒感染中中枢神经系统受累的潜在机制,特别是针对ANDV和PUUV。
elements_zh.main_results: 报告的神经系统特征包括头痛、头晕、意识状态改变、癫痫发作、局灶性缺陷以及周围神经病变,可能伴有视力障碍和畏光等眼部症状。神经影像学结果不一致且不特异,范围包括出血性或水肿性改变、丘脑或脑干异常以及脾状体病变。

elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 证据主要基于病例报告或病例系列,这可能限制结论的强度。研究结果表明,中枢神经系统受累的潜在机制具有中等程度的可信度,但致病性神经侵入仍不确定。

papers.title: Increasing spatial scale of analysis weakens and can mask the dilution effect for hantaviruses.
papers.abstract: Despite its major implications for biodiversity conservation and public health, the generality of a protective effect of biodiversity on zoonotic pathogen transmission (i.e., the dilution effect) remains strongly debated. This controversy may partly arise from the diversity of analytical approaches used, but also from the spatial scales at which studies are conducted. Here, we explicitly test whether increasing the spatial scale of analysis affects the detection of the relationship between hantavirus infection prevalence and rodent species richness, using a global dataset spanning multiple regions. Although the association between species richness and infection prevalence remains negative across all spatial scales, we show that the magnitude of the dilution effect progressively weakens as spatial aggregation increases and can become statistically non-significant at coarse spatial resolutions. These results, which are consistent across world regions, indicate that the dilution effect is likely a general feature of hantavirus-rodent systems, but that its empirical detection is highly sensitive to the spatial scale of analysis. Our findings highlight how large-scale spatial aggregation can mask underlying ecological processes and emphasize the need to carefully match spatial scale to the biological mechanisms under investigation when testing biodiversity-disease relationships. Finally, we discuss the ecological and methodological mechanisms that may obscure dilution effects and outline why scale-explicit approaches are essential for robust inference in biodiversity-disease research.

papers.title: Haemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome across three endemic clusters in Jiangxi Province, China’s middle Yangtze River region: long-term epidemiology and population-level changes after vaccination-programme initiation in Cluster I
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Haemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) remains an important public-health concern in endemic rural areas of China. Jiangxi contains three recognized endemic clusters, but their long-term temporal and age-related profiles, and the population-level changes following vaccination-programme initiation, have not been fully characterized. Methods We conducted a retrospective ecological study of HFRS surveillance records and county-level population denominators for 28 county-level units in Jiangxi from 2005 to 2024. We compared disease burden and seasonality across clusters, estimated long-term trends with Joinpoint regression, and characterized age–period–cohort (APC) patterns with an intrinsic-estimator model. In Cluster I, we used a staggered difference-in-differences design to examine changes in the incidence slope after county vaccination-programme initiation, incorporating rodent-surveillance data and sensitivity analyses of inference, functional form, treatment-effect heterogeneity, and county dependence. Results Across the three clusters, 7,570 cases were reported (crude incidence, 3.17 per 100,000). Cluster I had the highest burden (crude incidence, 7.00 per 100,000; age-standardized incidence rate [ASIR], 6.29). All clusters had bimodal seasonality. These findings have implications for public health strategies, emphasizing the importance of targeted interventions and continued surveillance. However, the ecological design and potential reporting biases limit the confidence in the results, resulting in a moderate evidence strength assessment.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 肾综合征出血热(HFRS)仍然是中国流行区农村地区重要的公共卫生问题。江西有三个公认的流行簇,但其长期的时间和年龄相关特征,以及在启动疫苗接种计划后的人群水平变化尚未被充分阐明。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 我们对江西省28个县级单位2005年至2024年的HFRS 监测记录和县级人口分母进行了回顾性生态学研究。我们比较了不同集群中的疾病负担和季节性,使用Joinpoint回归估计长期趋势,并利用内在估计模型描述了年龄–时期–队列研究(APC)模式。
elements_zh.methods: 在簇I中,我们采用交错的双重差分设计,考察县疫苗接种项目启动后发病率斜率的变化,结合鼠类监测数据以及对推断、函数形式、治疗效应异质性和县依赖性的敏感性分析。
elements_zh.main_results: Across the three clusters, 7,570 cases were reported (crude incidence, 3.17 per 100,000). Cluster I had the highest burden (crude incidence, 7.00 per 100,000; age-standardized incidence rate [ASIR], 6.29).
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该研究提供了关于肾综合征出血热长期流行病学的见解,并突出了疫苗接种计划对Cluster I地区疾病负担的影响,强调了持续监测和针对性干预措施的必要性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现为肾综合征出血热的防控提供了信息,特别是在已启动疫苗接种项目的地区,并强调了了解时间趋势和人口统计模式对于有效预防的重要性。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究受到其生态学设计的限制,这可能会掩盖个体层面的影响,且依赖于监测记录,这可能引入报告偏倚。由于这些限制,证据强度为中等。

papers.title: Generation and Characterization of the Human Anti-HTNV Antibody KJJ4
papers.abstract: Hantaan virus (HTNV) is the predominant causative agent of hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) in China, yet no specific antiviral therapy is currently available. Neutralizing antibodies (NAbs) represent a promising strategy, but most existing anti-HTNV NAbs are heterologous and carry immunogenicity risks. Here, two fully human antibodies from a previously established human anti-HTNV phage display library were generated and characterized. KJJ3, a VL-VL tandem antibody derived from clone 3–12, showed weak binding to inactivated HTNV and minimal neutralizing activity (IC50 = 27.12 μg/mL). However, KJJ4, an engineered IgG4 antibody derived from clone 4–19 and carrying the S108P hinge mutation to prevent Fab-arm exchange, bound inactivated HTNV antigen and recombinant glycoprotein Gn (residues 19–371) in a dose-dependent manner, with only weak binding to Gc. Surface plasmon resonance yielded an association rate constant of 4.70 × 103 M−1s−1, a dissociation rate constant of 3.06 × 10−3 s−1, and an equilibrium dissociation constant of 650 nM for monomeric Gn19–371. In a Vero E6 focus-reduction microneutralization assay, KJJ4 neutralized HTNV in vitro with an IC50 of 2.879 μg/mL. These data establish KJJ4 as a fully human anti-HTNV antibody with experimentally defined in vitro binding and neutralizing activity, warranting further evaluation in animal models of HTNV infection.

papers.title_zh: 人源抗HTNV抗体KJJ4的产生与表征
papers.source_body_en: Hantaan virus (HTNV) is the predominant causative agent of hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) in China, yet no specific antiviral therapy is currently available. Neutralizing antibodies (NAbs) represent a promising strategy, but most existing anti-HTNV NAbs are heterologous and carry immunogenicity risks. Here, two fully human antibodies from a previously established human anti-HTNV phage display library were generated and characterized. KJJ3, a VL-VL tandem antibody derived from clone 3–12, showed weak binding to inactivated HTNV and minimal neutralizing activity (IC50 = 27.12 μg/mL). However, KJJ4, an engineered IgG4 antibody derived from clone 4–19 and carrying the S108P hinge mutation to prevent Fab-arm exchange, bound inactivated HTNV antigen and recombinant glycoprotein Gn (residues 19–371) in a dose-dependent manner, with only weak binding to Gc. Surface plasmon resonance yielded an association rate constant of 4.70 × 103 M−1s−1, a dissociation rate constant of 3.06 × 10−3 s−1, and an equilibrium dissociation constant of 650 nM for monomeric Gn19–371. In a Vero E6 focus-reduction microneutralization assay, KJJ4 neutralized HTNV in vitro with an IC50 of 2.879 μg/mL. These data establish KJJ4 as a fully human anti-HTNV antibody with experimentally defined in vitro binding and neutralizing activity, warranting further evaluation in animal models of HTNV infection.
papers.abstract_zh: 汉坦病毒(HTNV)是中国肾综合征出血热(HFRS)的主要致病原因,但目前尚无特定的治疗手段。中和抗体(NAbs)代表了一种有前景的策略,但大多数现有的抗HTNV中和抗体均为异源性,并存在免疫原性风险。在此,我们从之前建立的人源抗HTNV噬菌体展示库中生成并表征了两种全人源抗体。来自克隆3–12的VL-VL串联抗体KJJ3对灭活HTNV的结合能力较弱,中和活性也较低(IC50 = 27.12 μg/mL)。然而,来自克隆4–19并携带S108P铰链区以防止Fab臂交换的工程化IgG4抗体KJJ4,能够以剂量依赖方式结合灭活HTNV抗原和重组糖蛋白Gn(残基19–371),仅对Gc有微弱结合。表面等离子体共振分析显示,单体Gn19–371的结合速率常数为4.70 × 103 M−1s−1,解离速率常数为3.06 × 10−3 s−1,平衡解离常数为650 nM。在Vero E6焦点减少微中和试验中,KJJ4在体外对HTNV表现出中和活性,IC50为2.879 μg/mL。这些数据确立了KJJ4作为具有实验定义的体外结合和中和活性的全人源抗HTNV抗体,值得进一步在HTNV感染的动物模型中评估。

news.content: Feedback | Friday, September 11, 2026 Skip Navigation DD News Menu Search Live Radio HI Top Stories National International Mann ki Baat Education Health Business & Economy Science & Tech Sports BRICS INDIA 2026 Environment Opinion Your browser does not support Javascript Tweets by DDNewslive Your browser does not support Javascript Home Top Stories Human to human hantavirus transmission suspected on cruise but risk to public low, WHO says 05/05/26 | 6:02 pm Share Your browser does not support JavaScript Human to human hantavirus transmission suspected on cruise but risk to public low, WHO says The World Health Organization said on Tuesday that it suspects some rare human to human transmission took place between close contacts on board a luxury cruise ship hit by seven confirmed or suspected hantavirus cases. A Dutch couple and a German national have died, while a British national was evacuated from the ship and is in intensive care in South Africa, officials said. Three more suspected cases affect people who are still on board, one of whom has a mild fever. The U.N. health body said its working assumption was that the initial case of the couple, who joined the boat in Argentina, were infected off the ship, perhaps while doing some activities such as bird watching, and that human-to-human transmission may have happened on board. The cruise ship hit by the deadly outbreak is marooned off Cape Verde – an island nation in the Atlantic off West Africa – and not allowed to put passengers ashore. The WHO said the focus now was to evacuate the two sick passengers still onboard to the Netherlands and then for the ship to continue to the Canary Islands. RISK LOW, BUT TRANSMISSIONS DO HAPPEN Human to human transmission is uncommon, and the WHO reiterated that the risk to the wider public was low from a disease typically spread from infected rodents that only rarely passes between humans. People are usually infected by hantavirus through contact with infected rodents or their urine, their droppings or their saliva. supplementary_news.content: Feedback | Friday, September 11, 2026 Skip Navigation DD News Menu Search Live Radio HI Top Stories National International Mann ki Baat Education Health Business & Economy Science & Tech Sports BRICS INDIA 2026 Environment Opinion Your browser does not support Javascript Tweets by DDNewslive Your browser does not support Javascript Home Top Stories Spain Confirms Preliminary Positive Hantavirus Test in MV Hondius Evacuee 12/05/26 | 10:26 am | Hantavirus Test | Positive Hantavirus Test | Spanish Health Minister Monica Garcia Share Your browser does not support JavaScript Spain Confirms Preliminary Positive Hantavirus Test in MV Hondius Evacuee Representational photo (Source: Xinhua/IANS) One of the 14 Spanish nationals evacuated from the hantavirus-hit cruise ship MV Hondius has preliminarily tested positive for the virus, Spanish Health Minister Monica Garcia said on Sunday. Garcia wrote on X on Monday (local time) that one of the Spanish passengers currently under isolation at Madrid’s Gomez Ulla hospital had tested preliminarily positive in a PCR test conducted upon arrival. “The person remains in isolation, without symptoms and in general good health, under continued clinical observation in accordance with established safety and epidemiological protocols,” she wrote. The other 13 Spaniards tested provisionally negative, while final results were expected in the coming hours, the minister said. According to health authorities and the World Health Organization (WHO), the outbreak is believed to involve the Andes strain of hantavirus, a variant known for possible person-to-person transmission through close contact. The virus is typically transmitted through exposure to infected rodent urine or droppings. The Spanish evacuees were transferred to Madrid as part of an evacuation operation launched after the MV Hondius arrived in Spain’s Canary Islands over the weekend, reports Xinhua news agency. Multiple confirmed and suspected cases have so far been linked to the outbreak, including passengers transferred to several countries for treatment and monitoring. The final group of evacuees left the ship on Monday after the vessel briefly docked at the Port of Granadilla on the Spanish island of Tenerife due to adverse weather conditions. The ship later departed for Rotterdam in the Netherlands. Meanwhile, the European Commission said Monday that it is coordinating and supporting national authorities’ response to a hantavirus outbreak, while the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC) assesses the risk to the general population in Europe as very low. Since Spain activated the EU Civil Protection Mechanism on May 6, the EU’s Emergency Response Coordination Centre has been facilitating the safe evacuation of people aboard the MV Hondius cruise ship, which was anchored off Tenerife. Five repatriation flights coordinated by the EU took place on Sunday and were carried out by France, Spain, the Netherlands, Greece and Ireland. A sixth and final flight, operated by the Netherlands, departed on Monday, according to the Commission. The EU is also mobilising response capabilities and stockpiles from its strategic reserve. A medical evacuation aircraft from the EU fleet, hosted by Norway, has been pre-positioned in Tenerife, while additional transport and logistics capacities, as well as protective equipment, are ready to be deployed if needed. The Emergency Response Coordination Centre has deployed a liaison officer to Tenerife to support on-site coordination with relevant authorities. The ECDC also deployed two experts from the EU Health Task Force to the ship before passengers disembarked. According to the Commission, the EU is working closely with EU members, countries participating in the Civil Protection Mechanism, the ECDC, the World Health Organization and G7 partners in responding to the outbreak. Commissioner for Equality, Preparedness and Crisis Management, Hadja Lahbib, said health threats can easily cross borders and coordination is therefore essential. supplementary_news.content: Feedback | Friday, September 11, 2026 Skip Navigation DD News Menu Search Live Radio HI Top Stories National International Mann ki Baat Education Health Business & Economy Science & Tech Sports BRICS INDIA 2026 Environment Opinion Your browser does not support Javascript Tweets by DDNewslive Your browser does not support Javascript Home Top Stories What is the hantavirus that killed three cruise ship passengers? 04/05/26 | 9:55 am | hantavirus | netharland Share Your browser does not support JavaScript What is the hantavirus that killed three cruise ship passengers? Three people have died and three are ill after a Netherlands-based cruise ship was hit by a suspected outbreak of hantavirus, authorities and media reports said on Sunday. Here is information about the virus. SPREAD BY RODENTS Hantavirus is primarily spread by rodents but can be transmitted between people in rare cases, according to the World Health Organization. People most typically become infected when virus in rodent droppings, saliva and urine becomes airborne, such as when areas where rats and mice have nested are swept out. According to The Lancet medical journal, the name comes from the Hantan River area of South Korea, where the virus was identified in the 1970s. CAN BE FATAL Hantavirus is a family of viruses that cause two illnesses, one that primarily affects the lungs and the other that attacks the kidneys. The first gets the most attention because it has a high fatality rate of about 40%. Hantavirus pulmonary syndrome, the respiratory illness, is most commonly found in North and South America. According to the Canadian government, about 200 cases of hantavirus pulmonary illness occur each year worldwide. Concert pianist Betsy Arakawa, wife of actor Gene Hackman, died from hantavirus pulmonary syndrome in New Mexico in 2025, according to autopsy results. SYMPTOMS Hantavirus usually begins with flu-like symptoms, such as fatigue and fever, one to eight weeks after exposure, according to the CDC. Four to 10 days later, coughing, shortness of breath and fluid in the lungs appear. Diagnosis in the first 72 hours of infection is difficult, the CDC says, so symptoms can easily be mistaken for flu. TREATMENT There is no specific therapy for hantavirus infection, so treatment focuses on supportive care including rest and fluids. Patients may need breathing support such as a ventilator. PREVENTION Experts say exposure to hantavirus can be minimized by deterring and eliminating rodents from areas where people are. Avoid vacuuming or sweeping dried droppings, which can aerosolize the virus. OffOn Stream on 3 dead in suspected hantavirus outbreak aboard a cruise ship: What to know The ship is off the coast of Cape Verde with 149 people on board. ByMary Kekatos May 4, 2026, 11:34 PM Share Follow ABC News on Google A rare rodent-borne disease may be behind a deadly outbreak aboard a cruise ship. There have been two laboratory-confirmed cases and five suspected cases of hantavirus, according to the World Health Organization (WHO). Of those seven people, three have died between April 11 and May 2 and one is currently in intensive care, according to the WHO. The WHO said Monday that investigations into the deaths and illnesses are ongoing, including further laboratory testing. Related The tragic deaths of Gene Hackman and Betsy Arakawa: A timeline The outbreak was reported on the MV Hondius, run by Oceanwide Expeditions, which was traveling between Argentina and the Canary Islands via Cape Verde. Currently, the ship is off the coast of Cape Verde with 149 people on board representing 23 different nationalities, Oceanwide Expeditions said in a press release on Monday. Here's what you need to know about the outbreak, what hantavirus is and how it spreads. This aerial picture shows a general view of the cruise ship MV Hondius stationary off the port of Praia, the capital of Cape Verde, on May 4, 2026. AFP via Getty Images Timeline of the outbreak South African health officials said in a statement on Monday that the first two deaths occurred in a married couple from the Netherlands. The 70-year-old male passenger became ill first with a fever, headache, abdominal pain and diarrhea starting on April 6. He passed away on board on April 11, according to Oceanwide Expeditions. No microbiological test were performed, according to the WHO. The deceased passenger's wife, 69, went ashore at St. Helena, a British territory in the South Atlantic Ocean, on April 24 with gastrointestinal symptoms, according to health officials. She collapsed at Johannesburg O.R. Tambo International Airport while trying to connect to fly home to the Netherlands on April 25, and was taken to a medical facility in nearby Kempton Park, according to health officials. She passed away on April 26, and her laboratory test results have come back positive for hantavirus, according to the WHO. Another patient, a British national, fell ill while the ship was traveling from St. Helena to Ascension, also a British territory, according to the South African health officials' statement. The passenger began showing symptoms on April 24 and he was medically evacuated from Ascension to South Africa on April 27, according to the WHO. "Despite medical treatment provided to him at Ascension, his condition did not improve and necessitated his medical evacuation to a South African private health facility in Sandton for further medical management," South African health officials said. The patient is currently in critical condition in isolation but receiving medical attention, according to health officials, who said his laboratory test results came back positive for hantavirus. A fourth passenger presented with pneumonia symptoms starting on April 28, according to the WHO. The German woman died on May 2 from causes not yet known, according to Oceanwide Expeditions. Related These US cities could see surge in disease-spreading pests this spring Meanwhile, there are three symptomatic people who remain on board the MV Hondius with suspected hantavirus cases, according to the WHO. Two crew members -- one of British nationality and one of Dutch nationality -- have acute respiratory symptoms. One has a mild illness and the other severe symptoms, with both requiring urgent medical care, Oceanwide Expeditions said. A third person also remains on board reporting high fever and/or gastrointestinal symptoms, according to the WHO. No other people with symptoms have been identified, Oceanwide Expeditions said Monday. Guests will not be disembarking in Cape Verde, expect for the three people who will be medically evacuated, according to Oceanwide Expeditions. "At this stage, a definitive disembarkation point for the remaining guests on board m/v Hondius has not been finalized," the company said Monday. "Sailing on to Las Palmas or Tenerife is being considered, where further medical screening and handling could take place, organized and supervised by the WHO and Dutch health services." The logo of shipping company Oceanwide Expeditions, which operates MV Hondius cruise ship, in Vlissingen, The Netherlands, May 4, 2026. Provicom/EPA/Shutterstock "Strict precautionary measures are in process on board, including isolation measures, hygiene protocols and medical monitoring. All passengers have been informed and are being supported," the company said. "We understand the considerable interest and concern and will share new information as soon as it has been verified." Popular Reads Iran live updates: US warplanes damaged in Iranian attack in Jordan, sources say 4 hours ago NTSB investigation underway after Amazon cargo plane crash leaves 5 dead, 5 injured Sep 8 Lindsay Clancy trial: Judge declares mistrial after emergency request denied Sep 4 WHO Director-General Dr. Tedros Ghebreysus said in a post on X on Sunday that the organization is working closely with both member states and ship operators in response to the suspected hantavirus cases. "WHO is facilitating medical evacuation of two symptomatic passengers, conducting a full risk assessment, and supporting affected people onboard," Ghebreysus wrote. What is hantavirus? Hantaviruses are a family of viruses that can cause serious illnesses and death, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). The viruses cause two syndromes: hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS) and hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS). HPS is mostly found in the Western Hemisphere, including the U.S., and HFRS is mostly found in Europe and Asia. Stock photo of a colorized electron micrograph of the Hantavirus. Alfred Pasieka/Science Photo Lib/STOCK PHOTO/Getty Images Surveillance for hantavirus in the U.S. began in 1993 during an outbreak in the Four Corners region, where Arizona, Colorado, New Mexico and Utah meet, the CDC said. Between 1993 and the end of 2023, 890 cases of hantavirus disease have been reported in the U.S., according to the CDC. Hantavirus became more widely known after being identified as the cause of death of the wife of actor Gene Hackman after the couple was found dead at their New Mexico home in February 2025. How does hantavirus spread? Hantaviruses are usually spread through rodents, including rats and mice, mostly from exposure to urine, droppings or saliva. Although the viruses can spread through a rodent bite or scratch, such infection is rare, the CDC says. Hantaviruses may also spread from person to person but that also is rare and only suspected for one subtype from South America, according to the WHO. What are the hantavirus symptoms? HPS symptoms typically appear from one to eight weeks after contact with the virus, with early signs including fever, fatigue and muscle aches, according to the CDC. Half of HPS patients will experience headaches, chills, dizziness, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea and abdominal pain. The CDC says that between four and 10 days after the initial phase of illness, the late symptoms will appear, including coughing, shortness of breath and tightness in the chest as the lungs fill with fluid. Related Gene Hackman's wife died of hantavirus; actor died of cardiovascular disease, Alzheimer's: Officials About 38% of people who develop HPS respiratory symptoms may die from the disease, according to the CDC. Symptoms of HFRS usually develop one to two weeks after exposure and typically include intense headaches, fever, chills, back pain, abdominal pain, nausea and vomiting, the CDC says. Later symptoms may include low blood pressure, lack of blood flow, internal bleeding and acute kidney failure. Depending on the virus causing the infection, fatality among infected humans can range from less than 1% to as high as 15%, the CDC says. What hantavirus treatments are available? No specific treatment is available for hantavirus infection, with the CDC recommending patients receive supportive care such as rest, hydration and treatment of symptoms. Because HPS can cause breathing difficulties, patients may need breathing support, such as intubation, the CDC says. Because HFRS can disrupt kidney function, infected patients may need dialysis to remove toxins from the blood, according to the CDC. OffOn Stream on WHO says suspected hantavirus cluster 'is not the start of a COVID pandemic' There are 12 suspected cases so far. ByMary Kekatos and Zoe Magee May 7, 2026, 4:39 PM Share Follow ABC News on Google An epidemiologist from the World Health Organization (WHO) said Thursday that the suspected hantavirus cluster aboard a cruise ship is not the beginning of another COVID-19 pandemic. Eight cases are currently being reported by the WHO, including five laboratory-confirmed cases and three suspected cases. Of those eight cases, three have died. Dr. Maria Van Kerkhove, an infectious disease epidemiologist and acting director of epidemic and pandemic management at the WHO, was asked during a press conference what the difference was between this cluster and the early days of the COVID pandemic. Related Officials in Arizona, Georgia monitoring some hantavirus cruise ship passengers who have returned to US "I want to be unequivocal here. This is not SARS-CoV-2. This is not the start of a COVID pandemic. This is an outbreak that we see on a ship," Van Kerkhove said. Van Kerkhove explained that hantavirus doesn't spread in the same way that coronaviruses do, but rather through "close, intimate contact." Most hantaviruses don't transmit from person to person. "The actions that are being taken on board [the ship] are precautionary to prevent any onward spread," she added. Health personnel assisting patients onto a boat from the cruise ship MV Hondius, while stationary off the port of Praia, the capital of Cape Verde, May 6, 2026. AFP via Getty Images There appears to be two confirmed cases and four suspected cases that have not been added to the WHO's official count yet. The Ministry of Health, Welfare and Sport confirmed that two patients infected with the virus are currently hospitalized in the Netherlands, one at Radboud University Medical Center and the other at Leiden University Medical Center. Additionally, two Singapore residents who were on board the ship are currently being monitored. Singapore's Communicable Diseases Agency said it was notified of the individuals on May 4 and 5. "They have been isolated at the National Centre for Infectious Diseases, where they are being tested for hantavirus. The risk to the general public in Singapore is currently low," the agency said. The agency added that test results are pending, with one resident having a runny nose. The other is asymptomatic. The French Health Ministry also issued a statement on Thursday that a French national has been tested after they displayed mild symptoms. This person had been in contact with one of the confirmed cases. Related 3 people waiting to be medically evacuated from cruise ship at center of suspected hantavirus outbreak Three deaths have been recorded so far, including a married Dutch couple. The 70-year-old male patient died on April 11, and his body was taken off the ship on the island of St. Helena on April 24. His 69-year-old wife disembarked on the same day, and her health rapidly deteriorated. She died at a South Africa hospital on April 26. A third passenger, a German woman, presented with pneumonia symptoms starting on April 28, according to the WHO. The woman died on May 2 from causes not yet known, according to Oceanwide Expeditions, which operates the cruise ship. The WHO said 29 people disembarked on St. Helena on the same day that the body of the Dutch male patient and his wife disembarked. They traveled to 12 countries: Canada, Switzerland, Germany, Denmark, Great Britain, St. Kitts and Nevis, Netherlands, New Zealand, Singapore, Sweden, Turkey and the United States. Popular Reads Iran live updates: US warplanes damaged in Iranian attack in Jordan, sources say 4 hours ago NTSB investigation underway after Amazon cargo plane crash leaves 5 dead, 5 injured Sep 8 Lindsay Clancy trial: Judge declares mistrial after emergency request denied Sep 4 The disembarked guests have all been contacted by Oceanwide Expeditions. In the U.S., local authorities in five states -- Arizona, California, Georgia, Texas and Virginia -- are monitoring the disembarked passengers and are conducting contact tracing, None have shown signs of illness at this time. Anais Legend, technical lead for viral hemorrhagic fevers at WHO, said during the press conference on Thursday that "step-by-step guidance is being developed" for the disembarked passengers and that the WHO is coordinating with national authorities. Anyone with any signs of symptoms will be isolated while other passengers have their risk exposure evaluated. The cruise ship MV Hondius, carrying passengers suspected of having cases of hantavirus on board, leaves Praia, Cape Verde, May 6, 2026. Reuters Public health experts said they expected a more robust response from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) and the National Institutes of Health. "CDC would typically be asked by WHO to, or by a country to, help in technical assistance," Dr. Carlos del Rio, an H. Cliff Sauls distinguished professor of medicine at the Emory University School of Medicine, told reporters on Thursday. Typically, CDC teams would be deployed to an area, he said, and the teams would perform contact tracing and interviews and conduct an outbreak investigation. "I would envision by now, many, many days ago, we would have seen ... a team from CDC deployed to the area," he added. Related 3 dead in suspected hantavirus outbreak aboard a cruise ship: What to know Dr. Jeanne Marrazzo, CEO of the IDSA, added that she would have expected a CDC press briefing, an alert from the agency's Health Alert Network or information from the NIH on potential treatments in the pipeline that could receive emergency use authorization to help treat hantavirus patients. Marrazzo said she is not aware that conversations about potential therapies at NIH aren't happening but it "does not give me a lot of assurance or reassurance that we're not hearing about any of it." The CDC posted a statement on X on Wednesday on behalf of NIH Director and acting CDC director Dr. Jay Bhattacharya that read, "Our hearts go out to the passengers aboard the cruise ship M/V Hondius and their families during this difficult time. Our CDC team began coordinating with domestic and international partners as soon as we were notified of a hantavirus situation." The statement said there is "clear, written health guidance to the American passengers through the State Department" and that the CDC "will continue to update as more information becomes available and remains committed to protecting the health and safety of the American public." The agency also published a statement on its website stating that the Trump administration "is closely monitoring the situation" and that the Department of State "is leading a coordinated, whole-of-government response including direct contact with passengers, diplomatic coordination, and engagement with domestic and international health authorities." The CDC also said the risk to the American public is "extremely low." The WHO said during Thursday's press briefing that the U.S. is coordinating with the global health agency in a technical capacity. Because the cluster is limited and confined to a cruise ship, the "idea of sending messages across the world and panicking everyone is not required," said Dr. Abdirahman Mahmoud, director of the WHO's health emergency alert and response operations. He added that the WHO is "informally" aware that contact tracing has been done of the U.S. passengers who disembarked last month and are back home. Reynolds Listen 0:00 / 0:00 Key Takeaways Surveyed clinicians reported 85% perceived hantavirus coverage as exaggerated, while 77% rated population risk low/non-meaningful and 62% observed increased patient questions. Most management centered on counseling: 89% prioritized explaining transmission, alongside reassurance about limited person-to-person spread and guidance to reduce rodent exposure. Federal sentencing addressed a 2017–2022 scheme using call centers, ghost telehealth encounters, and remotely controlled pharmacies across 75+ sites to generate prescriptions irrespective of consent. Insurers paid >$758M on $1.97B in claims; operators used aliases, shell entities, encrypted communications, straw owners, and international laundering, with an alleged leader still abroad. Longitudinal surgeon data showed near-10% eight-year attrition, peaking in 2020; mid-career departures were greatest, rural representation fell 10.5% to 8.5%, and female share rose to 28.6%. SHOW MORE The top news stories in medicine today. Advertisement Physicians say hantavirus media coverage is outpacing the actual risk A Sermo survey of 104 doctors found 85% believe current coverage exaggerates the public threat, even as 62% report a rise in patient inquiries. More than eight in ten physicians say media coverage of hantavirus is overstating the actual risk to the general public, even as patient anxiety climbs in the wake of recent headlines, according to a new Sermo survey of 104 U.S. physicians across infectious disease, internal medicine, pulmonology and emergency medicine. Seventy-seven percent of respondents rated the current risk to the general public as low or non-meaningful, consistent with CDC data showing fewer than 50 hantavirus cases are typically reported in the U.S. annually. Yet 62% of physicians said they have already seen an increase in patient inquiries about the virus. Physicians described a familiar dynamic: heightened media coverage driving patient concern without a corresponding change in underlying disease risk. The most common clinical response was education on transmission, cited by 89% of respondents, followed by reassurance about low transmission risk and prevention guidance around rodent exposure. Three sentenced in Moscow-based $2B telemedicine fraud scheme targeting U.S. insurers The criminal organization ran ghost telemedicine visits, fraudulent prescriptions and remotely controlled pharmacies across more than 75 locations nationwide. Three members of a Moscow-based criminal organization have been sentenced to federal prison for their roles in a nearly $2 billion health care fraud conspiracy that used sham telemedicine visits, fraudulent prescriptions and remotely operated pharmacies to defraud private insurers, with many patients never receiving the medications billed in their names. Anthony Santamaria received 10 years; co-defendants Hershel Tsikman and Hafizullah Ebady received 120 and 97 months, respectively. Between 2017 and 2022, the organization used call centers in Utah and later Russia to contact insurance beneficiaries and generate prescriptions regardless of whether they agreed to receive medications, then submitted more than $1.97 billion in fraudulent claims through over 75 pharmacies acquired across New York, New Jersey, Pennsylvania, Texas, Michigan and Alabama. Private insurers paid out more than $758 million before the scheme was uncovered. The defendants concealed their involvement through aliases, encrypted communications, shell companies and straw owners, laundering proceeds internationally. The organization's alleged leader, U.S. citizen Brian Sutton, is believed to be living abroad and remains at large. Three additional co-defendants are awaiting sentencing. Nearly 1 in 10 surgeons leave the profession within 8 years, study finds Mid-career surgeons are most at risk, and attrition spiked sharply in 2020 during the COVID-19 pandemic. Nearly 10% of surgeons left clinical practice within an eight-year period, with attrition highest among mid-career surgeons and in subspecialties including oral and maxillofacial surgery, obstetrics and gynecology, and plastic and reconstructive surgery, according to a new study published in the Journal of the American College of Surgeons. Researchers at Ohio State University analyzed data on more than 224,000 surgeons across 19 specialties from 2013 to 2023 and found overall attrition rates held steady until 2020, when they rose sharply, likely driven by pandemic-era retirements. Five-year cumulative attrition was highest in oral and maxillofacial surgery at 25.1%, followed by obstetrics and gynecology at 23.2% and plastic and reconstructive surgery at 19.3%. The share of surgeons practicing in rural areas shrank from 10.5% to 8.5% over the decade, while the percentage of female surgeons rose from 21.2% to 28.6%. "Surgical attrition is a real problem, and we need to address it in a nuanced and tailored way," said co-author Timothy Pawlik, M.D., M.P.H., Ph.D., FACS, of Ohio State's Wexner Medical Center. Published : 9/5/2026 10:07| Lifestyle powered by UKHSA identified a suspected case of Hantavirus in a British national on the remote South Atlantic island of Tristan da Cunha. This follows a confirmed outbreak aboard the cruise ship MV Hondius. The UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) announced on Friday that a third British citizen is suspected of being infected with the rare Hantavirus. The individual was located on Tristan da Cunha, a remote British Overseas Territory in the southern Atlantic Ocean. While laboratory confirmation is pending for this specific case, the agency confirmed that two other British nationals have already tested positive for the virus following an outbreak on a cruise ship. Fatalities and confirmed infections The outbreak originated aboard the MV Hondius, a Dutch-flagged vessel traveling from Argentina. As of Friday, the deadly pathogen has claimed three lives: a married couple from the Netherlands and a German national. The UKHSA reports that five cases have been laboratory-confirmed so far, with several other passengers and crew members under investigation for suspected symptoms including fever, respiratory distress, and pneumonia. Repatriation measures The MV Hondius is expected to dock at Tenerife in the Canary Islands on Sunday. UKHSA officials stated that British nationals currently on board who do not show symptoms will be repatriated to the UK via air travel. Upon arrival, these individuals will be required to undergo a mandatory 45-day self-isolation period. This extended timeframe, which exceeds the typical 14-day quarantine, is designed to account for the long incubation period of the Andes hantavirus variant identified in this outbreak.
